emails.content:
Welcome to the first Nano Flips Newsletter!

​
​

As we dove into putting together the first newsletter, several questions popped up.

​

  1. Should we do an expensive site? Or more affordable one
  2. How many people will actually open up the email?
  3. Is this a terrible idea?

​
Well, questions 2 and 3 are up in the air. But question 1? That one was decided for us. We are going to look at whatever good opportunities come our way! So make sure the newsletter is marked as important and not going to the promotional folder of Gmail (90% of you use Gmail - wow google has a foothold).

​

Today we are going to look at a website that could be bought for $5000 (It's currently listed under that at the time of writing this).

​

With a little effort. we are going to get more like $20k+ out of it in the next 12 months. Don't worry this is pretty simple and easy, part-time stuff.

​

Let's dive in!

​

The Site

​

​

Its a motorcycle site, you can check it out here​

​

​

Lets look at several reasons that this site might be a decent buy, that could be ripe for flipping:

​

  • Its monetized with Adsense
  • It has had stable traffic over the last 12+ months
  • It has a niche focus
  • Its getting traffic from several sources
  • It has a DA of 43
  • Traffic is coming from tier one countries
  • Seller has a good reputation

​

Now, let's take a look at the things we don't like about it.

​

  • Most of the traffic is coming from sharing on social media (takes time)
  • Its traffic to images
  • Revenue is pretty low (not massive growth to squeeze out without growing traffic
  • WE WANT TO MAKE SURE BUYER IS INCLUDING ALL SOCIAL MEDIA PROFILES
  • Traffic isn't SUPER stable

​

There are several things we can do here to make it more valuable. Let's take a look.

​

The Plan

​

  • We are going to change out Adsense for a premium ad network! We are going to probably go with something like Ezoic. The larger ones won't take the site. But we might try! Automatad, Adpushup, Adthrive, Mediavine, Lockerdome. There are more, but that would be a good start. This is probably going to increase revenue by 50% or more.

​

  • Build out a blog! 2 points of attack here, first is going to be finding low-hanging keywords, that we can rank for easily using a tool like Ahrefs or SEMrush. We are going to write an original piece on Harleys or motorcycles 2-3x a week, this will increase traffic AND revenue, we might even to content to monetize with Amazon affiliates. This is ALSO going to allow us to sell a sponsored post ever other week as well. With a DA of 43, getting $100 or so shouldnt be too hard. Make sure your ratio of fresh content to sponsored posts is high. Google doesn't like you selling these things.

​

  • Make a Facebook Group! I know, you thought I was going to say make a newsletter! I dont think the traffic is compelling enough currently unless you LOVE motorcycles and you find it fun. Build a pop up that direct people to your FB group where they can chat and share their love of motorcycles together. I would say its fair to get 300+ new people a month, who share it with their friends as well. I would think a reasonable goal here is 5-10k members by the end of the year. Later on you can sell sponsorship space in the group, or charge people to list their bikes for sale.

​

If you are good at this, THIS WILL BE A MASSIVE MONEY MAKER FOR YOU. But let's assume you aren't, you still are going to pull $200 a month from selling a sponsor banner ad slot at the top of the FB group.

​

The Profit

​

1.Well first off the site was making $156 a month before from Adsense. ASSUMING WE DONT GROW THE SITE AT ALL (we will), that becomes $234 a month at a 50% increase in revenue with a premium ad network.

​

2. The new blog exists! In fact, we are probably going to go greatly increase traffic with lots of great new content. But let's assume we just keep doing what we were before and making image posts to Pinterest and the like. BUT we are selling 2 sponsored posts a month at $100 each. That's $200 more a month.

​

3. The new Facebook group exists! Let's be conservative and assume you don't have enough members or sell sponsorship at all until 6 months in. Later on, though we are making $200 a month!

​

If we add all those up we get a new net monthly income of $634 a month.

​

For the first 6 months, we are only earning $434 a month.

​

For the year our new total income is $6408, you paid $5000, so your cash on cash return 128.16%

​

We now have a site that we are going to sell for 3x yearly net rev OR $19,224

​

When you add those together and subtract costs, the net profit in 12 months is.......

​

$20,632.00

​

Now I know what you are all saying, "ONLY $20k"!? Well first off guys, this is pretty conservative. This also probably could be done in 4 hours a week. OR 200 hours over the year or $100 an hour for your time. NOT a terrible side income, that's for sure.

​

Well, that's it! That's it for issue #1 of Nano Flips. Keep your eyes peeled, as these will go out as opportunities arise, sometimes they will be $20k profits, sometimes $1 million or more.

​

​

In fact, we are probably going to start recognizing real revenue from amazon associates (It currently makes a tiny amount according to their P&L, we can say $25 a month), but let's assume we don't grow that with new content, even though we will. ​

3. We have a better lead capture form. I'm not going to speculate on what that does for revenue. Could be $0, could be $500+ because of how we monetize the list. Let's say $0 to be safe.

​

​

​

​

​

The next 9 months comes out to $13106.25

​

​

​

When you add those together and subtract costs, the net profit in 12 months is.......

Here we go:

​

"Hi, I’m Sean Markey, an SEO expert that’s learned everything the hard way and someone that’s built multiple affiliate sites to 4-5 figures per month, as well as sold a site for well into six-figures.

​

In this piece, I’m going to take you through at a very high level, how to buy a domain with a robust history and valuable backlinks already built, how to build out a site that should get some fairly quick traction, and why you want to do this. Here we go.

​

Why Build on Domains With a History

​

Every day tens-of-thousands of domain names expire. Most of them are terrible garbage names that people register with the grandest of intentions, but never get around to building on. Some of them, however, used to be businesses that someone pinned all their hopes and dreams on, spent thousands of hours creating and publishing content, building links through hard-earned PR. In the end, entropy gets us all, and as the hilarious and very successful comedian Conan O’Brien said: “eventually, all our graves go unattended.”

​

So it goes with businesses! But their loss is your incredible gain.

​

Rather than building a site on a brand new domain that’s never been seen in the world before, one in which people (and search engine algorithms) inherently do not trust because it is so new, so untested, you can pick up the carcass of someone’s failed dream and build something amazing upon it. Buying a site that has hundreds or thousands of links going to it and is already indexed in Google’s algorithm lets you cut to the front of the line, essentially, and build something that gets search engine ranking traffic a lot more quickly.

​

How to Find a Domain With SEO Juice

​

There’s definitely an art to finding domains with existing authority among all the trash expiring every day, and I’m going to give you the 80/20.

​

1. Look at GoDaddy Auctions and Sort by Number of Bids

​

GoDaddy is the place to go for valuable expiring domains because they’ve got the biggest volume. Several other registrars funnel their expiring domains through the GoDaddy auction system, so just as you wouldn’t pan for gold in a swamp, don’t overthink where to look for good expiring domains—GoDaddy is where it’s at.

​

Once you visit auctions.godaddy.com, you’ll need to sign up for an auction account—that’s $4.99 per year. Now you can bid on domains!

​

To find the auctions that are valuable (either because the domain itself is valuable, or because it has valuable backlinks, you just need to do this:

​

Click “Advanced Search”

​

Select “contains” from the drop-down menu and leave it blank (top left)

​

Click “expiring auction” (bottom left)

​

Click “search” (bottom right)

​

Now, just sort the list of domains you get by “number of bids.” Put any domains that seem to have a lot of bids but is clearly not a premium one-word domain name into your favorite SEO tool (I prefer ahrefs.com) and see what kind of links it already has.

​

This is going to change some people’s lives in incredible ways. Check it out here. Or below ⬇️

​

​

​

2. Use ExpiredDomains.net to Find Other Good Opportunities

​

This popular (and free!) tool gets a lot of use from people looking to find expired domains with authority. You can sort by number of backlinks, number of organic search volume, and other interesting filters.

​

You’ll get better at searching the more you do it, so practicing with this site is highly recommended if you’re a beginner.

​

3. Use a Paid Tool Like DomCop.com or spamzilla.io to Find Domains

​

If you’ve got some money to throw at the problem, these two paid tools are highly recommended. If you know what you’re doing (by which I mean, if you have SEO experience) you can sort by a ton more metrics here than on expireddomains.net. These tools will give you a feed of all expiring domains at ALL platforms, and let you search by Moz DA, Ahrefs DR, Majestic CF/TF, or other amazing filters like “topical relevancy of backlinks.”

​

What to Do Once You’ve Acquired a Domain With Juice

​

A mistake a lot of domain-buyers make is to just go in once they have control of the domain and 301 it at the register to another site they are trying to rank well (this is because a large majority of people buying expired domains do so with the intention of helping a site they’re already building vs. building new).

​

But I’m going to assume you’re looking for a project to build out and not boost another, so that’s how the advice will flow.

​

First, you want to get the domain live. My suggestion is always “never skimp on hosting.” Find a nice WP managed host for your Wordpress site and push it live. Next, you want to get SOMETHING live on it as soon as you can. This is because the longer the site is down, the more links it loses and the more authority gets washed away. So your first goal should be to get a site live with like, a few blog posts, a home page, an about/contact page, at minimum.

​

Now you can take things a bit slowly, since you’re not in danger of losing authority and trust.

​

Do some keyword research and find some ideal keywords to write about, keywords you want to rank for. The authority your site has will help you with this. No tricks here, just… build a good site, consistently post content, and try and build on a clean, attractive design.

​

Finally, look in a tool like Ahrefs and find the most linked-to pages on the site…these will probably be the main pages on the site-that-used-to-be-built on this domain, or any article that went a bit viral. Most likely, these pages won’t be relevant to the site you’re building, but you can still capture some value.

​

Here’s what you do:

​

Find these well-linked-to pages using Ahrefs’ “best pages by links”

​

Ignore the home page, find old inner pages with links

​

Download a plugin like “Redirection” and redirect these names with a lot of links to /blog page, or to a similar other “general” page.

​

That’s it.

​

Now you’ve a site that has existing authority and is well-poised to start getting organic traffic from all the great content you’re now posting. "
